# @0k/folio

The npm wrapper for [x0k-folio](https://github.com/0k-dot-computer/x0k-folio):
prebuilt binaries for projects that want the tools without a Rust toolchain.
The tools themselves — the folio/v1 document format, the `x0k-tangle`
tangler/checker, and the `x0k-folio-cli` query surface — are documented in
[the repository](https://github.com/0k-dot-computer/x0k-folio) and its
[integration guide](https://github.com/0k-dot-computer/x0k-folio/blob/main/guides/INTEGRATING.md).

## This package cannot install yet

**No tagged release has been cut**, so there is nothing for the postinstall to
download and `npm install @0k/folio` fails. That is the honest state of it:
the wrapper and its release workflow are written and tested, and the first tag
has not been pushed. Until it is, the way to the binaries is a Rust toolchain
and a C compiler (for the tree-sitter grammars):

```sh
cargo install x0k-tangle    # the tangler and checker, published on crates.io

git clone https://github.com/0k-dot-computer/x0k-folio
cd x0k-folio && cargo build --release -p x0k-folio-cli    # the query CLI, from the clone
```

## What it will install

```sh
npm install -g @0k/folio
```

Three commands: `folio` and `x0k-tangle` are the tangler and checker, and
`x0k-folio` is the query CLI.

The package carries no binary of its own. `install.js` runs on install, reads
the platform table in `package.json`, fetches the one release asset built for
your platform, and verifies it twice before it is used — against a SHA-256
digest pinned into this package when the release was cut, and against the
release's SLSA build provenance. **If either check does not hold, the install
fails rather than proceeding**, and an unrecognized platform is an error
rather than a silent fallback. The binaries land in the package's `vendor/`
directory, which is written on your machine and is neither committed nor
published.

Supported platforms are Linux (x64, arm64), macOS (x64, arm64) and Windows
(x64).
